The use of Gaussian visible variables is useful to handle real data and has been suggested since the beginning of the theory . However the learning and retrieval capabilities of the fully visible BM with Gaussian units are not as good as its pm1 counterpart at low-load , and at high-load they are totally useless . Restricted architectures are more interesting. RBMs with Gaussian visible and latent variables have been used for instance for factor analysis and collaborative filtering . In general training, through e.g. contrastive divergence, is slower than that in a Bernoulli-Gaussian machine and also retrieval is less pronounced . Independently on their performances, Gaussian BMs are of great theoretical relevance from the viewpoint of spin glasses, since their simpler mathematical structure helps our understanding of the, much more complicated, discrete models. Previous results on the model have been obtained in and . In the authors achieve the same result as in our Theorem and prove much more: fluctuations of the free energy are shown to be Gaussian in high temperature and Tracy-Widom for low temperature. nodes.statement: Legendre transforms are where the idea of equivalence of ensembles exploits and more precise statements are given in Theorem below. A Gaussian prior of N units concentrates on a N-dimensional sphere of radius proportional to sqrt N. To find the optimal radius we slice up the Gibbs measure at the level of the Gaussian prior and look for the most relevant contribution to the free energy. This strategy yields naturally a variational principle of the Legendre type relating the spherical and Gaussian free energies. Moreover we identify the square radius of the optimal sphere R^2 and the variance of the Gaussian model theta^-1 as Legendre conjugate variables.
